question: Which of the following is the oldest newspaper of India still in circulation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay Samachar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bombay Samachar** is the oldest continuously published newspaper in India.
 
• It was first published on **1 July 1822**.
 
• The newspaper primarily serves the Parsi community and is published in the **Gujarati language**.
 
• **Bombay Samachar** started as a weekly publication but later became a daily newspaper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Udant Martand**

 
 
• It was the first Hindi-language newspaper published in India.
 
• Launched on 30 May 1826 in Calcutta, it was a weekly newspaper.
 
• Despite its historical significance, it ceased publication in December 1827.
 
 
 
• **Samachar Darpan**
 
 
• It was the first Bengali-language newspaper published in India.
 
• Started on 23 May 1818 by the Serampore Mission Press, it played a significant role in journalism in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Amrita Bazaar Patrika**
 
 
• It was one of India's oldest newspapers, founded in 1868.
 
• Originally a Bengali weekly, it became a daily and switched to English in 1878.
 
• It was known for its strong nationalist stance during the Indian independence movement.
 
• Unfortunately, it ceased publication in 2004.
